input.question: Why are we able to cross our eyes and unable to do the opposite?
input.ground_truth: Some people can do just that. Otherwise, it just fucks with your brain trying to put two images from both eyes at different angles together. Crossing out eyes focuses on something in front of us. Making the eyes look in their own direction doesn't do us any good for survival, so the skill never really evolved

Question: Why are we able to cross our eyes and unable to do the opposite?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine your eyes are like two little toy balloons on your face. When you want to cross your eyes, you can make the balloons (your eyes) move toward each other and meet in the middle. That’s easy because your eyes can turn inwards.

But if you try to make your eyes go the other way—like, really far apart, so they point away from each other as much as possible—it’s hard or even impossible. That’s because your eyes are connected to muscles that are really good at bringing them together, but not as good at pulling them apart too much. If your eyes went too far apart, you wouldn’t be able to see things clearly, and it might even hurt!

So, you can easily cross your eyes (bring them together), but it’s hard to make them go the other way (pull them apart a lot). That’s how your eyes are made to work best!
